values.note: $12.15 a night: the Indiana DNR's first-come, first-served primitive rate for state forest campgrounds.

sites.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/greene-sullivan-state-forest/ ('each of the 100 family campsites of Narrow Lake, Wampler Lake, and Reservoir #26'), read 2026-11-02

facilities.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/greene-sullivan-state-forest/ ('Sites have pit toilets and seasonal drinking water available'; 'A dumping station is also available'), read 2026-11-02

booking.source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/forestry/properties/greene-sullivan-state-forest/ ('campsites are available on a first-come, first-serve basis. Self-check-in stations are located in each campground or at the forest office'), read 2026-11-02

note: Three separate family campgrounds on reclaimed strip-mine lakes: Narrow Lake (this pin), Reservoir #26 and Wampler Lake. The horse camp near Ladder Lake is excluded. Rent-a-camp cabins are separate. --Claude
summary: Base $12-12.15 -> $12.15; 100 sites, FCFS confirmed; pit toilets, seasonal water, dump added. Removed the note's '5 electric RV sites' (page says primitive). Forest is three campgrounds 2-4 km apart: split lead. Lakefront stands at Narrow Lake; pin is in the lake.
flags: SPLIT LEAD: the DNR trail map shows three separately placed and named campgrounds, each with its own road: Narrow Lake (off Shady Lane by E CR 350 S, ~39.0332,-87.2557), Reservoir 26 Campground (off the county road at Goodman Rd, ~39.0179,-87.2419, loop and playground visible on imagery, ~2.1 km from Narrow), Wampler Campground (east side, ~4 km from Narrow; approx. 39.015,-87.217 scaled from the map; imagery there is full canopy, no loop visible, so don't treat as pinned). Distances from imagery and the map scaled against two road crossings. The page gives only the combined 100, no per-campground split.

PIN: 39.0338,-87.2567 sits on the water of the lake, about 110 m from the Narrow Lake camp. Under 250 m but in the lake: corrected to the loop, 39.0332,-87.2557 (loop and parked RVs visible on imagery; individual pads partly).

ELECTRIC: the old note claimed '5 electric RV sites (P1-P3 ...)'. The DNR page says 'Primitive (class C)' for all of it and nothing about electric or those site numbers. I removed the claim from the note and wrote no hookups value because 'no electric' isn't stated in as many words. Fee follows the primitive rate.
PHONE (stored empty): 812-648-2810, forest office, on the DNR page and Google (Google lists the forest overall: 4.2 from 44).

WATER: lakefront stands for the Narrow Lake loop. On imagery at 0.44 m/px, parked RVs on the spur north of the loop sit ~20-25 m from the shore across open grass, no road between. The lake is well over 5 acres (roughly 10, measured). Overpass was down; figures are imagery estimates. Other two campgrounds not judged; Reservoir 26 sits below a levee with a road on it, so it wouldn't inherit this call if split.
FIT: page silent on rig length. Trailers and motorhome-sized units are visible parked on the Narrow Lake loop's gravel. Fishing-lake ramps are electric-motor only; no bearing on camping.

ADVISORIES: trail section closed for reclamation activities; not the campground. Google reviews read: 'Campgrounds are nice' (4 months ago), a cabin complaint (3 months ago, AC failed in a rent-a-camp cabin, not the campground).
SEASON not stated for the campground; left alone. Ownership state stands.
